title: TreeView
description: A tree root plus the view read under it: the serializable form of what a reader reads (interfaces spec §B.3, item S1). Its CID (`TreeView::cid`, the dag-cbor CID of the canonical encoding) is the placement need key for a tree (`NeedKey::TreeView`, R1: per tree root and view, never per blob). Two encodings, the BlobLink rule: in DAG-CBOR the root is tag 42 and each path an array of byte-string components (the root path is the empty array); in JSON, shaped here, the root is the CID string and each path is slash-joined UTF-8 with "" for the root. Wire shape: this schema is the source of record; eprfs_core::TreeView (elohim/eprfs/eprfs-core/src/view_decl.rs) is its Rust mirror, not yet pinned to it by a test (follow-on: an eprfs-serve contract test that serializes TreeView values and validates them here). The Rust codec is the authority only for the canonical DAG-CBOR bytes and the CID (`TreeView::cid`). Source of truth: the reader's request, from which it is derived per read; a value object with no entry type of its own (Category C as a wire value; its identity is content-derived, never a slug). Not to be confused with enums/closure (the open | closed posture toward silence, finding 7).

root.description: The tree root: a CIDv1 over sha2-256 with the dag-cbor codec (a tree node), base32 lower case. In JSON a string; in DAG-CBOR tag 42 (BlobLink).

ViewPaths.title: ViewPaths

items.description: One view path: slash-joined UTF-8 path components under the root, or "" for the root itself. No leading or trailing slash, no empty component, no NUL, and no `.` or `..` component (refused per component by the `not`). A non-UTF-8 component cannot be spelled in JSON at all; the canonical DAG-CBOR form carries components as byte strings, and the Rust decoder refuses a non-UTF-8 path in the human-readable form with TreeError::InvalidView.

ViewPaths.description: A view: the path prefixes under a tree root that a reader reads, the paths alone (no root). `[""]` is the whole tree (`View::whole()`). The canonical form is the NORMALIZED view: sorted component-wise (not by the slash-joined string: '-' 0x2d sorts before '/' 0x2f) and an antichain (no path covered by another), so that `TreeView::cid` is a function of the view (finding B7). JSON Schema cannot express component-wise order or the antichain rule; the Rust and TypeScript decoders refuse a non-canonical list (TreeError::InvalidView), and the shared vector in eprfs-core's fixtures/tree-vectors.json pins ["a","a/b"] as refused on decode and as normalizing to ["a"] through TreeView::new with the same cid. Referenced by the app manifest's `needs` block as the shape of `closure` (titled StartSet there), which carries paths only: the release record binds the root.
